title: KV hit-economics strategy: stratified hit-modeling, TTL annealing, and canary rollback plan
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We are seeing uneven KV cache economics across tenants and routes. A small set of prefixes produce most hits but current static TTLs and naive key shaping expose us to either wasted memory (over-retention) or high cold-start token costs (under-retention). This ticket defines a practical, instrumented approach to produce per-prefix TTL recommendations, an annealing schedule for safe configuration changes, and an automated canary + revert plan that integrates with rollout tooling and SRE alerts.

Goal: Produce a lightweight hit-economics model and a repeatable safe-apply workflow that enables product teams to reduce per-token spend while preserving latency SLOs. Deliverables: 1) modeling notebook and CLI to compute per-prefix recommended TTL ranges and expected cost delta; 2) a templated annealing schedule and canary runbook; 3) automation hooks for safe apply/auto-revert based on signal thresholds and synthetic probes.
acceptance_criteria: A modeling notebook (Python) that inputs per-prefix traffic histograms and outputs a recommended TTL range and expected cost delta in tokens/hour.
A set of PromQL queries and dashboards that surface: prefix hit-rate, eviction rate, average response latency, backend QPS, and cost delta estimation in near-real time.
A documented annealing schedule (percent rollout steps, time windows) and explicit revert triggers based on SLO regressions, latency tail shifts, and error spikes.

An automated canary runner (script + GH Action) that applies TTL changes to a controlled cohort, executes synthetic probe prompts, evaluates metrics against thresholds, and either advances the rollout or reverts.
Playbook entries for on-call: steps to inspect telemetry, manually revert, and escalate to runtime/infra if necessary.
Benchmarks showing >=10% token cost reduction in a non-trivial workload subset without >5% P95 latency increase (or with documented trade-offs).
proposed_solution: 1) Build a stratified hit-economics model: split prefixes into cohorts by activity (hot/warm/cold) using decaying-count windows and compute marginal cost-per-hit vs backend-call cost. 2) For each cohort compute a Pareto frontier of TTL choices: retention vs mem-footprint vs hit-rate. 3) Create an 'annealing plan' that applies TTL changes incrementally using percent-based rollout (5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%) with a minimum observation window (e.g., 60m per step) and conservative backoff. 4) Implement automated probes: pairs of synthetic prompts per prefix to measure end-to-end latencies, token billing delta, and functional correctness. 5) Wire the canary runner to existing rollout service (console rollouts) with a gated auto-revert that triggers on defined metric regressions. 6) Publish recommendations and a CLI for teams to propose initial TTLs that are safe and explain expected delta in tokens and cost.
implementation_steps: Gather sample telemetry schema and create a lightweight aggregator (daily histogram of prefix counts, unique users, average response length).
Prototype stratified hit-model in a Jupyter notebook (use reservoir sampling to avoid heavy data transfer).
Define cohort boundaries (e.g., top 1% hot, next 9% warm, rest cold) and compute marginal hit curves per cohort.
Design an annealing schedule templated YAML that rollout tooling can consume (percentages, min observation duration, success criteria).
Implement canary runner: GH Action + small reverse-proxy layer that injects modified TTL response headers for the canary cohort and executes synthetic probes.

Add PromQL snippets to the runtime dashboards and set temporary alert rules for canary experiments (P95 latency delta > 4x baseline, backend error increase > 15%, hit-rate drop > configured threshold).
Run shadow experiments on a 2% traffic slice to validate model predictions and calibrate thresholds before enabling auto-advance in the runner.
Document the playbook for SRE and runtime-ops including manual revert CLI and investigation checklist.
Rollout to first non-critical tenant and capture cost/latency tradeoffs, then iterate on the model hyperparameters (cohort boundaries, anneal timings).
canary_plan: Target cohort: choose stable, well-instrumented route with mid-level traffic (not top hot nor bottom cold).
Step 0: Dry-run compute expected impact and record baseline for 24h.
Step 1: Apply TTL change to 2% traffic (canary flags) and run 60m observation window. Execute synthetic probes at 1/min.
Step 2: If no triggers, move to 10% and observe 2h. If still healthy, 40% for 6h, then 100% with staggered group-by-region to avoid global spikes.

Auto-revert triggers: P95 latency increases by >10% absolute or 2x relative to baseline, backend 5xx increase > 10%, hit-rate drop larger than model-predicted confidence band. If any trigger fires, automatically revert to prior TTL and notify on-call with runbook link.
Manual checks: sanity-check synthetic probe outputs for content correctness and distributional shift in token generation length.
telemetry_queries: PromQL: sum by(prefix) (rate(kv_cache.misses[5m])) and sum by(prefix) (rate(kv_cache.hits[5m])) to compute live hit-rate per prefix.
PromQL: increase(kv_cache.evictions[1h]) / increase(kv_cache.sets[1h]) to surface eviction pressure.
SQL (clickhouse): SELECT prefix, quantile(0.95)(latency_ms) as p95, sum(tokens) as tokens_hour FROM requests WHERE time > now()-1h GROUP BY prefix;
Estimated cost delta formula (not implemented in code): delta_tokens_hour = predicted_miss_increase * avg_response_tokens; cost_delta_usd = delta_tokens_hour * unit_token_cost_usd.
rollback_triggers: Automated: P95 latency delta > 10% absolute OR >2x relative baseline within observation window.
Automated: backend 5xx rate increase > 10% sustained for 3 consecutive windows.
Automated: observed hit-rate falls outside predicted confidence interval by >5 percentage points for the cohort.
Manual: downstream product owner reports functional regression or generation quality degradation in >3 customer cases within observation window.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: model overfits to historical burst patterns and underestimates miss-rate during novel workloads. Mitigation: require a shadow 2% run for 72h and conservative confidence multipliers before full rollout.
Risk: automated rollback loops due to noisy telemetry. Mitigation: use smoothing windows, require sustained triggers (>=3 windows) and include a cooldown period before re-attempts.

Risk: multi-tenant interference where one tenant's TTL change increases eviction pressure for others. Mitigation: cohort selection must be tenant-aware and we schedule region-scoped rollouts when multi-tenant nodes present.
Risk: incorrect key shaping causing cache fragmentation. Mitigation: include a key-stability score in the model (e.g., churn metric) and avoid aggressive changes for unstable keys.
